answer_text:
Let

\[
t=2x+5,\qquad y=f(t)=\frac{\ln t}{t}.
\]

Since \(t\) is linear in \(x\), \( \frac{dt}{dx}=2 \), so

\[
\frac{d^3}{dx^3}f(t)=f'''(t)\left(\frac{dt}{dx}\right)^3=8f'''(t).
\]

Now compute the derivatives with respect to \(t\):

\[
f(t)=\frac{\ln t}{t}
\]

\[
f'(t)=\frac{1-\ln t}{t^2}
\]

\[
f''(t)=\frac{2\ln t-3}{t^3}
\]

\[
f'''(t)=\frac{11-6\ln t}{t^4}
\]

Therefore,

\[
y'''=8\cdot \frac{11-6\ln(2x+5)}{(2x+5)^4}
\]

\[
y'''=\frac{88-48\ln(2x+5)}{(2x+5)^4}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{88-48\ln(2x+5)}{(2x+5)^4}}
\]
